The test image shows young corn seedlings (V2-V3 stage) in the field. Key observations:
- Very young seedlings emerging from soil
- The middle plant has a dead/dark stub at the top (dead growing point)
- Some browning/dead tissue at the base of plants
- Otherwise leaves appear green

This could be Stewarts wilt (seedling wilt phase), Bacterial stalk rot, or Crazy top. Let me check reference images for the top candidates.

Looking at the test image:
- Very young seedlings (V1-V2 stage) in field
- The middle plant has a dark/dead stub at the top — the growing point appears dead
- Plants on either side appear healthy green
- Some brownish dead material at plant bases

**Analysis:**
- **Crazy_top**: Shows bushy leafy proliferation at tassel — wrong growth stage, doesn't match
- **Bacterial_stalk_rot**: Affects more mature plants with soft slimy stalk rot and collapse — doesn't match young seedlings
- **Stewarts_wilt**: Has a seedling wilt phase near emergence that kills the growing point — matches young seedling stage with dead growing tip; the reference collage shows young seedlings at a similar growth stage with dying plants

The dead, dark stub at the top of the center seedling is consistent with Stewarts wilt seedling wilt phase, where the growing point is killed near emergence. The surrounding plants look healthy, matching the pattern of scattered plant death typical of Stewarts wilt.
